newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends higher on winterkill concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends higher on winterkill concerns.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures ended higher Tuesday on concerns that bitterly cold temperatures this week might damage the U.S. winter wheat crop, floor traders said.
"Whether or not we see any winterkill later on, it's still a market factor right now," said one commission house trader.

Temperatures were forecast to sink below zero this weekend in Kansas, which is the top wheat-producing state in the U.S. The bitterly cold temperatures combined with a lack of snow could produce winterkill in the dormant crop, traders said.
Cargill was a heavy late buyer in on the CBOT and in KCBT, and that buying helped push prices near session highs.
In other trade, LIT sold two million bushels March, FIMAT Futures Inc bought 500,000 bushels March and O'Connor Grain bought one million bushels March.

Bearish factors in Tuesday's trade included news that South Korea, citing high prices, passed on a feed wheat tender for 105,000 tonnes. Some also were disappointed that Egypt has yet to come in for 500,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat.
CBOT wheat futures ended up 3-1/2 to four cents per bushel, with March up four at $3.92-1/2 and May up 2-3/4 at $3.70.
In wheat options trade, Cargill Investor Services sold 200 March $4.00 calls, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 10,000 contracts, down from the 14,887 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
